meta.title: The Graph You Never Wrote
meta.subtitle: One write fence and seventeen read fences per component type — every edge in your job graph falls out of that array

views.label: You declare, you never wire
views.note: The query already said which component types you read and which you write. That declaration is the only input the dependency system gets.

views.label: The hazard rule, in one line
views.note: A reader waits on writers. A writer waits on writers and on every reader. Two readers of the same type never wait for each other.

views.label: The handle goes back on the board
views.note: Your returned handle is written into the fence slots of every type you touched, so the next system inherits the edge without asking.

views.label: When the slots run out
views.note: Seventeen readers is the ceiling. The eighteenth forces those seventeen to be combined into one handle, which frees the slots again.

cards.title: The hazard rule, from the source
items: For each type you read: take that type's write fence · ComponentDependencyManager.cs:239
For each type you write: take the write fence and every read fence · line 246
Combine them all into one handle and hand it back · line 266
So two readers of the same type are never ordered against each other

cards.title: What never becomes an edge
items: A zero-sized type that is not enableable is dropped from both lists · CalculateReaderWriterDependency.cs:13

cards.title: When each step happens
items: Before your update the system marks itself as needing the fences · SystemState.cs:581
